svg.title: Precision and ambiguity impose different aperture constraints
svg.desc: Synthetic mathematical illustration. See the caption and adjoining model for assumptions and interpretation.
svg.text: Precision and ambiguity impose different aperture constraints
1 GHz; λ = 0.300 m. Sector ±60°; local uncertainty ≤ 0.5°.
One baseline cannot satisfy both constraints at the supplied energy
At ρ = 100: precision needs 1.0943 m; ambiguity needs d < 0.1732 m.
Short baseline needs ρ = 5321.9: 53.22 ms at zero offset, beyond the brief.
Use two simultaneous baseline lengths to supply different information.
Long-baseline aliases: Δu = λ/dₗ = 0.25, where u = sin θ.
u = 0.25 and u = 0.50 give identical long-baseline wrapped phase.
The short comparison supplies branch information; it is not a precision substitute.
Single plane-wave manifold, correct orientation and calibrated state are supplied.
Illustrative model • no measured receiver data
